summary: UI components for sign-in, sign-up and password recovery: accessible validation, correct autocomplete, submitting state and error messages. They contain no authentication logic.
whenToUse: Sign-in, sign-up and password recovery pages connected to your identity provider or backend.
whenNotToUse: If you use an identity provider with hosted pages (e.g. Entra ID, Auth0, Keycloak login): redirect to those.
As a security system: client-side validation does not replace server-side validation.

props.name: AuthLayout: headingLevel
props.description: Title level (use 2 if the page already has an h1).

props.name: AuthLayout: aside
props.description: Side panel shown from 1024 px (image, testimonial). Don't put essential content in it: it is hidden on small screens.

props.name: AuthLayout: fullHeight
props.description: Fills the viewport height (100dvh); false to embed it in a section or preview.

props.name: LoginForm: onSubmit
props.description: Called after validation. If it returns a Promise, the button shows the loading state until it settles.

props.name: LoginForm: forgotPasswordHref / showRememberMe
props.description: Recovery link and “Stay signed in” checkbox.

props.name: SignUpForm: showName, passwordMinLength, confirmPassword, termsLabel
props.description: Name field, minimum length (in Unicode characters), password confirmation, required terms checkbox.

props.name: PasswordResetForm: onSubmit, defaultEmail, isSubmitted, successMessage
props.description: Shows a neutral message after a successful submission; isSubmitted makes it controlled.

props.name: error
props.description: Error returned by your service (wrong credentials, attempt limit), announced with role="alert".

props.name: isPending
props.description: Controlled submitting state; otherwise driven by the onSubmit Promise.

props.name: providers / footer / submitLabel
props.description: Alternative sign-in (SSO, passkey) below the “or” separator, trailing content and button text.

props.name: defaultValues
props.description: Initial values (never the password for SignUpForm).

inherits: Props of the react-aria-components Form (action, method, validationErrors, className…), except onSubmit and validationBehavior. Ref forwarded to the <form>.

keyboard.action: Moves through the fields in visual order.
Submits the form; if there are errors, focus moves to the first invalid field.

accessibility: Visible labels, with descriptions and errors linked to the field (aria-describedby) and announced.
autocomplete: username/email, current-password on sign-in, new-password on sign-up, name: password managers work.
PasswordInput lets users reveal the password; pasting is never blocked.
While submitting, the button stays focusable and announces progress (react-aria isPending); double submissions are ignored.
Server errors use role="alert"; the password recovery confirmation uses role="status".
responsive: The card is fluid up to 28rem with padding that shrinks on narrow screens; the aside panel appears from 1024 px.
No fixed widths: works at 320 px and at 200% zoom.
customization: For forms with different fields, compose Form, TextField, PasswordInput and Checkbox inside AuthLayout.
System messages are translated via LocaleProvider (auth* keys).
commonMistakes: Revealing whether an account exists (“email not registered”): use neutral messages, as PasswordResetForm does.
Letting onSubmit reject the Promise to show an error: handle the error and pass it to error. A rejected Promise is propagated (submitting state reset) and surfaces as an unhandled error.
Requiring password confirmation when the field already lets users reveal the text (NIST SP 800-63B doesn't require it): that's why confirmPassword defaults to false.
Treating these components as an authentication system: rate limiting, MFA, sessions and CSRF protection are the backend's responsibility.
